claim: The vertebrate retina contains an interplay between retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), amacrine (AC), and bipolar (BP) cells that establishes a synaptic layer called the inner plexiform layer (IPL).
source: In the vertebrate retina, an interplay between retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), amacrine (AC), and bipolar (BP) cells establishes a synaptic layer called the inner plexiform layer (IPL).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of retinal anatomy.

claim: The retinal circuit conveys signals from photoreceptors to visual centers in the brain.
source: This circuit conveys signals from photoreceptors to visual centers in the brain.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of retinal function.

claim: Striatin-interacting protein 1 (Strip1) is a core component of the striatin-interacting phosphatases and kinases (STRIPAK) complex.
source: Striatin-interacting protein 1 (Strip1) is a core component of the striatin-interacting phosphatases and kinases (STRIPAK) complex, and it has shown emerging roles in embryonic morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Loss of Strip1 causes defects in IPL formation in zebrafish.
source: Using zebrafish, we show that loss of Strip1 causes defects in IPL formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: In strip1 mutants, RGCs undergo dramatic cell death shortly after birth.
source: In strip1 mutants, RGCs undergo dramatic cell death shortly after birth.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by TUNEL assay data in Figure 3.

claim: AC and BP cells invade the degenerating RGC layer in strip1 mutants, leading to a disorganized IPL.
source: AC and BP cells subsequently invade the degenerating RGC layer, leading to a disorganized IPL.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by imaging data in Figure 2.

claim: Zebrafish Strip1 interacts with its STRIPAK partner, Striatin 3 (Strn3).
source: Mechanistically, zebrafish Strip1 interacts with its STRIPAK partner, Striatin 3 (Strn3), and both show overlapping functions in RGC survival.
evidence: This is supported by Co-IP/MS data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Strip1 and Strn3 show overlapping functions in RGC survival.
source: Mechanistically, zebrafish Strip1 interacts with its STRIPAK partner, Striatin 3 (Strn3), and both show overlapping functions in RGC survival.
evidence: This is supported by morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Loss of Strip1 or Strn3 leads to activation of the proapoptotic marker, Jun, within RGCs.
source: Furthermore, loss of Strip1 or Strn3 leads to activation of the proapoptotic marker, Jun, within RGCs, and Jun knockdown rescues RGC survival in strip1 mutants.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6C-F.

claim: Jun knockdown rescues RGC survival in strip1 mutants.
source: Furthermore, loss of Strip1 or Strn3 leads to activation of the proapoptotic marker, Jun, within RGCs, and Jun knockdown rescues RGC survival in strip1 mutants.
evidence: This is supported by morpholino rescue experiments shown in Figure 6G-J.

claim: Strip1 is required for RGC dendritic patterning.
source: In addition to its function in RGC maintenance, Strip1 is required for RGC dendritic patterning, which likely contributes to proper IPL formation.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell imaging data in Figure 1G and transplantation experiments in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The retina is a highly organized neural circuit that comprises six major classes of neurons, assembled into three cellular layers with two synaptic or plexiform layers between them.
source: The retina is a highly organized neural circuit that comprises six major classes of neurons, assembled into three cellular layers with two synaptic or plexiform layers between them.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as established knowledge about retinal anatomy.

claim: Retinal lamination is conserved among vertebrates and is critical for processing visual information.
source: Lamination is conserved among vertebrates and is critical for processing visual information (Baden et al., 2020; Nassi and Callaway, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: RGCs are the first-born retinal neurons, which extend their axons to exit the eye cup and innervate visual centers in the brain.
source: RGCs are the first-born retinal neurons, which extend their axons to exit the eye cup and innervate visual centers in the brain (D'Souza and Lang, 2020, Robles et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: When RGCs are absent or exhibit defects in axon projections in mouse and zebrafish models, vision is compromised.
source: In mouse and zebrafish models, when RGCs are absent or exhibit defects in axon projections, vision is compromised (Kay et al., 2001; Moshiri et al., 2008; Rick et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Strip1 was first described as one of the core components of the striatin-interacting phosphatases and kinases (STRIPAK) complex.
source: It was first described as one of the core components of the striatin-interacting phosphatases and kinases (STRIPAK) complex (Goudreault et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The STRIPAK complex is an evolutionarily conserved supramolecular complex with diverse functions in cell proliferation, migration, vesicular transport, cardiac development, and cancer progression.
source: The STRIPAK complex is an evolutionarily conserved supramolecular complex with diverse functions in cell proliferation, migration, vesicular transport, cardiac development, and cancer progression (He et al., 2010; Hwang and Pallas, 2014; La marca, 2019; Madsen et al., 2015; Neisch et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Several STRIPAK components participate in dendritic development, axonal transport, and synapse assembly.
source: In addition, several STRIPAK components participate in dendritic development, axonal transport, and synapse assembly (Chen et al., 2012; Li et al., 2018; Schulte et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In Drosophila, Strip is essential for axon elongation by regulating early endosome trafficking and microtubule stabilization.
source: In Drosophila, Strip (a homolog of mammalian Strip1/2) is essential for axon elongation by regulating early endosome trafficking and microtubule stabilization (Sakuma et al., 2014; Sakuma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Loss of mouse Strip1 causes early mesoderm migration defects leading to embryonic lethality.
source: On the other hand, loss of mouse Strip1 causes early mesoderm migration defects leading to embryonic lethality (Bazzi et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: At 4 days post-fertilization (dpf), rw147 mutant embryos have small eyes, lower jaw atrophy, and cardiac edema.
source: At 4 days post-fertilization (dpf), rw147 mutant embryos have small eyes, lower jaw atrophy, and cardiac edema (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: rw147 mutants show defects in retinal lamination, in which retinal layers, especially in the inner retina, fluctuate in a wave-like pattern.
source: rw147 mutants also show defects in retinal lamination, in which retinal layers, especially in the inner retina, fluctuate in a wave-like pattern (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The rw147 mutation is lethal by 6 dpf due to cardiac edema.
source: The rw147 mutation is lethal by 6 dpf due to cardiac edema.
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results.

claim: Mapping of the rw147 mutation revealed a missense mutation in exon 7 of the strip1 gene.
source: Mapping of the rw147 mutation revealed a missense mutation in exon 7 of the strip1 gene of the rw147 mutant genome (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: strip1crisprΔ10 mutants show similar morphology and retinal lamination defects to those of strip1rw147 mutants.
source: strip1crisprΔ10 mutants show similar morphology and retinal lamination defects to those of strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Knockdown of Strip1 using translation-blocking morpholinos (MO-strip1) phenocopied strip1rw147 mutants.
source: Likewise, knockdown of Strip1 using translation-blocking morpholinos (MO-strip1) phenocopied strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: Wild-type Strip1, but not the mutant form, rescued the retinal defects of strip1rw147.
source: Wild-type Strip1, but not the mutant form, rescued the retinal defects of strip1rw147 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I.

claim: Strip1 was expressed in RGCs and ACs at 2 dpf.
source: Strip1 was expressed in RGCs and ACs at 2 dpf (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: strip1 mRNA is maternally and zygotically expressed and by 2 dpf, expression becomes restricted to the eyes, optic tectum, and heart.
source: In situ hybridization shows that strip1 mRNA is maternally and zygotically expressed and by 2 dpf, expression becomes restricted to the eyes, optic tectum, and heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: In wild-type retinas, IPL and OPL are evident at 3 dpf.
source: In wild-type retinas, IPL and OPL are evident at 3 dpf.
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results.

claim: IPL shows abnormal morphology in strip1rw147 mutants at 3 dpf, whereas OPL is relatively normal.
source: In contrast, IPL shows abnormal morphology, whereas OPL is relatively normal in strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In wild-type siblings, a rudimentary IPL was formed as early as 52 hr post-fertilization (hpf); however, it was less defined in strip1rw147 mutants.
source: In wild-type retinas, a rudimentary IPL was formed as early as 52 hr post-fertilization (hpf); however, it was less defined in strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: In wild-type siblings, RGCs and ACs normally extend their dendrites toward the IPL; however, strip1rw147 mutants show randomly directed dendritic patterns of RGCs and ACs.
source: In wild-type siblings, RGCs and ACs normally extend their dendrites toward the IPL; however, strip1rw147 mutants show randomly directed dendritic patterns of RGCs and ACs (Figure 1G, H).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1G, H.

claim: BPs of strip1rw147 mutants show misrouted axons and abnormal dendritic branching.
source: In wild-type siblings, BPs normally extend their axons and dendrites toward IPL and OPL, respectively; however, BPs of strip1rw147 mutants show misrouted axons and abnormal dendritic branching (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 1I.

claim: RGCs are severely reduced in strip1rw147 mutants at 3 dpf.
source: Live imaging of 3-dpf retinas revealed that RGCs are severely reduced in strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mutant ath5+ RGCs are reduced, reaching only 7.45% ± 2.88% of total retinal area, compared to 24.18% ± 1.48% in wild-type siblings.
source: we quantified RGC area compared to total retinal area and found that mutant ath5+ RGCs are reduced, reaching only 7.45% ± 2.88% of total retinal area, compared to 24.18% ± 1.48% in wild-type siblings (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There was no significant change in the number of ptf1a+ ACs between strip1rw147 mutants and wild-type siblings.
source: On the other hand, there was no significant change in the number of ptf1a+ ACs between strip1rw147 mutants and wild-type siblings (Figure 2A, C).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2A, C.

claim: In strip1rw147 mutants, a significant fraction of ptf1a+ ACs were abnormally located in the GCL.
source: However, in strip1rw147 mutants, a significant fraction of ptf1a+ ACs were abnormally located in the GCL (Figure 2A, arrowheads in bottom panels, and Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2A, D.

claim: In wild-type siblings, most strong Pax6+ cells were in the INL, and only 9.84% ± 4.13% were in the GCL.
source: In wild-type siblings, most strong Pax6+ cells were in the INL, and only 9.84% ± 4.13% were in the GCL (Figure 2E, G).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2E, G.

claim: In strip1rw147 mutants, a significant percentage of Pax6+ cells (44.26% ± 17.8%) was in the GCL.
source: However, in strip1rw147 mutants, a significant percentage of Pax6+ cells (44.26% ± 17.8%) was in the GCL (Figure 2E, G).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2E, G.

claim: In wild-type, 100% of Prox1+ cells were in the INL.
source: In wild-type, 100% of Prox1+ cells were in the INL (Figure 2H, J).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2H, J.

claim: 10.6% ± 6.26% of Prox1+ cells were abnormally located in the GCL in strip1rw147 mutants.
source: However, 10.6% ± 6.26% of Prox1+ cells were abnormally located in the GCL in strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 2H, J).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2H, J.

claim: In zebrafish, RGC genesis starts in the ventronasal retina at 25 hpf, spreads into the entire retina by 36 hpf and is completed by 48 hpf.
source: In zebrafish, RGC genesis starts in the ventronasal retina at 25 hpf, spreads into the entire retina by 36 hpf and is completed by 48 hpf (Avanesov and Malicki, 2010; Hu and Easter, 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In strip1rw147 mutants, RGCs are normally produced at 36 hpf; however, apoptosis occurred in the GCL at 48 hpf.
source: In strip1rw147 mutants, RGCs are normally produced at 36 hpf; however, apoptosis occurred in the GCL at 48 hpf (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The number of apoptotic cells in GCL reached its highest level at 60 hpf, and apoptotic cells were eliminated by 96 hpf.
source: The number of apoptotic cells in GCL reached its highest level at 60 hpf, and apoptotic cells were eliminated by 96 hpf (Figure 3A, B).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3A, B.

claim: RGC population was significantly lower in strip1rw147 mutants than in wild-type siblings at 60 hpf and progressively reduced by 96 hpf.
source: Accordingly, RGC population was significantly lower in strip1rw147 mutants than in wild-type siblings at 60 hpf and progressively reduced by 96 hpf (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary quantitative finding stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: strip1rw147 mutant donor RGCs underwent apoptosis in wild-type host retinas.
source: TUNEL of transplanted retinas at 60 hpf revealed that strip1rw147 mutant donor RGCs underwent apoptosis in wild-type host retinas (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding from cell transplantation experiments stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3D–F.

claim: Strip1 is cell autonomously required for survival of RGCs.
source: To determine whether Strip1 cell autonomously promotes RGC survival, we conducted cell transplantation from strip1rw147 mutant donor cells into wild-type host embryos at the blastula stage. TUNEL of transplanted retinas at 60 hpf revealed that strip1rw147 mutant donor RGCs underwent apoptosis in wild-type host retinas (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by cell transplantation data in Figure 3D–F.

claim: The majority of mutant RGCs transplanted in wild-type retina show irregular neurite projections.
source: However, the majority of mutant RGCs transplanted in wild-type retina show irregular neurite projections, apically directed processes (presumably dendrites) do not project to a uniform layer and show distant abnormal branching (asterisks, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Strip1 is cell autonomously required for neurite morphogenesis of RGCs.
source: Taken together, Strip1 is cell autonomously required for survival and neurite morphogenesis of RGCs.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by cell transplantation data.

claim: At 48 hpf, there were no apparent differences in position or morphology of RGCs and ACs between wild-type siblings and strip1rw147 mutants.
source: At 48 hpf, there were no apparent differences in position or morphology of RGCs and ACs between wild-type siblings and strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 4A and Figure 4—videos 1; 2).
evidence: This is a primary observation from time-lapse imaging stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In strip1rw147 mutants at 52 hpf, RGCs started to disappear, creating an empty spot in the GCL.
source: In strip1rw147 mutants at 52 hpf, RGCs started to disappear, creating an empty spot in the GCL (Figure 4A, asterisks).
evidence: This is a primary observation from time-lapse imaging stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: At 59 hpf, ACs started to invade the empty spaces in the GCL in strip1rw147 mutants.
source: At 59 hpf, ACs started to invade the empty spaces in the GCL (Figure 4A, arrowheads).
evidence: This is a primary observation from time-lapse imaging stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Loss of RGCs triggers infiltration of ACs into the GCL in strip1rw147 mutants.
source: Thus, loss of RGCs triggers infiltration of ACs into the GCL in strip1rw147 mutants.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by time-lapse imaging data.

claim: When mutant ACs were transplanted into wild-type host retinas, most donor ACs were normally positioned in the INL and extended dendrites toward the IPL.
source: When mutant ACs were transplanted into wild-type host retinas, most donor ACs were normally positioned in the INL and extended dendrites toward the IPL, as in the case of wild-type donor ACs transplanted into a wild-type host retina (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: This is a primary observation from cell transplantation experiments stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4C, D.

claim: When wild-type donor ACs were transplanted to mutant host retinas, they showed irregular neurite projection with many somas abnormally located toward the basal side, resulting in IPL formation defects.
source: On the other hand, as with mutant donor ACs transplanted into mutant host retinas, when wild-type donor ACs were transplanted to mutant host retinas, they showed irregular neurite projection with many somas abnormally located toward the basal side, resulting in IPL formation defects (Figure 4C, D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary observation from cell transplantation experiments stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4C, D.

claim: Strip1 is not required in ACs for IPL formation.
source: These data suggest a non-cell autonomous function of Strip1 in ACs for IPL formation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by cell transplantation data.

claim: Strip1 is not required in BPs for neurite projection to the IPL.
source: Thus, Strip1 is not required in ACs or BPs for neurite projection to the IPL, although we do not exclude the possibility that Strip1 is cell autonomously required in a small subset of ACs and BPs to regulate dendritic branching and neurite extension.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by cell transplantation data.

claim: Strip1-mediated RGC maintenance is essential for proper neurite patterning of ACs and BPs, and for subsequent IPL formation.
source: Taken together, it is likely that Strip1-mediated RGC maintenance is essential for proper neurite patterning of ACs and BPs, and for subsequent IPL formation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by cell transplantation data.

claim: Six proteins were enriched only by the wild-type form of Strip1, 5 of which are components of the STRIPAK complex.
source: Six proteins were enriched only by the wild-type form of Strip1, 5 of which are components of the STRIPAK complex (Figure 5C, D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from Co-IP/MS experiments stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5C, D.

claim: Only strip1 and strn3 mRNA are abundantly expressed in retinal cells at 2 dpf.
source: we analyzed previously published single-cell RNA sequencing data on transcriptomes from zebrafish embryonic retinas at 2 dpf (Xu et al., 2020), and found that only strip1 and strn3 mRNA are abundantly expressed in retinal cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding from analysis of published scRNA-seq data stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–I.

claim: There was a significant increase in apoptotic cells in the GCL of strn3 morphants at 60 hpf.
source: We observed a significant increase in apoptotic cells in the GCL of strn3 morphants at 60 hpf (Figure 5E, F).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5E, F.

claim: Strn3 knockdown leads to a significant reduction in RGCs at 60 and 76 hpf.
source: This leads to a significant reduction in RGCs at 60 and 76 hpf, as assessed by the ath5:GFP signal (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5G–I.

claim: Strn3 is a Strip1-interacting partner that shows similar roles in promoting RGC survival.
source: Taken together, Strn3 is a Strip1-interacting partner that shows similar roles in promoting RGC survival.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by Co-IP/MS and morpholino knockdown data.

claim: Compared to wild-type siblings, strip1 mutants had 131 significantly upregulated genes and 75 downregulated genes.
source: Compared to wild-type siblings, strip1 mutants had 131 significantly upregulated genes and 75 downregulated genes (Figure 6A, log2FC > |1|, and False Discovery Rate (FDR) < 0.05).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RNA sequencing stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Most downregulated genes in strip1 mutants were markers of RGCs, like isl2b, pou4f3, and tbr1b.
source: Most downregulated genes were markers of RGCs, like isl2b, pou4f3 (also known as brn3c), and tbr1b, which reflects the reduction in RGCs.
evidence: This is a primary observation from RNA sequencing stated in the Results.

claim: Many significantly upregulated genes in strip1 mutants were related to apoptosis, oxidative phosphorylation, cellular response to stress, and the MAP kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway.
source: On the other hand, many significantly upregulated genes were related to apoptosis, oxidative phosphorylation, cellular response to stress, and the MAP kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway (Figure 6A, B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary observation from RNA sequencing stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6A, B.

claim: There were several genes commonly upregulated in strip1 mutant eyes, adult zebrafish RGCs following ONI, and adult eyes after optic nerve crush, namely, jun, atf3, gap43, stmn4, sox11b, and adcyap1b.
source: Indeed, there were several genes commonly upregulated in all three models, namely, jun, atf3, gap43, stmn4, sox11b, and adcyap1b (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from comparative analysis stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Strip1-deficient zebrafish RGCs share a similar stress response with adult RGCs following ONI.
source: These findings suggest that Strip1-deficient zebrafish RGCs share a similar stress response with adult RGCs following ONI.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by comparative transcriptomic analysis.

claim: In strip1 mutants, jun was among the top upregulated stress response markers.
source: In strip1rw147 mutants, jun was among the top upregulated stress response markers.
evidence: This is a primary observation from RNA sequencing stated in the Results.

claim: At 54 hpf, strip1rw147 mutants showed significantly elevated levels of p-Jun compared to wild-type siblings, specifically localized in RGCs.
source: At 54 hpf, strip1rw147 mutants showed significantly elevated levels of p-Jun compared to wild-type siblings. This elevation is specifically localized in RGCs visualized with zn5 antibody (Figure 6C, D).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6C, D.

claim: p-Jun was significantly elevated in RGCs of strn3 morphants at 49 hpf compared to control-injected embryos.
source: Likewise, p-Jun was significantly elevated in RGCs of strn3 morphants at 49 hpf compared to control-injected embryos (Figure 6E, F).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6E, F.

claim: At 60 hpf, apoptosis was significantly inhibited in the GCL of strip1rw147 mutants injected with MO-jun, compared to strip1rw147 mutants injected with a standard control morpholino.
source: At 60 hpf, apoptosis was significantly inhibited in the GCL of strip1rw147 mutants injected with MO-jun, compared to strip1rw147 mutants injected with a standard control morpholino (Figure 6G, H).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6G, H.

claim: At 76 hpf, RGCs were partially but significantly recovered in strip1rw147 mutants injected with MO-jun, compared to strip1rw147 mutants injected with a standard control morpholino.
source: Accordingly, at 76 hpf, RGCs were partially but significantly recovered in strip1rw147 mutants injected with MO-jun, compared to strip1rw147 mutants injected with a standard control morpholino (Figure 6I and J).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6I, J.

claim: Strip1 and Strn3 suppress Jun-mediated apoptotic signaling in RGCs.
source: Taken together, Strip1 and Strn3 suppress Jun-mediated apoptotic signaling in RGCs.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by Jun knockdown rescue experiments.

claim: Bcl2 overexpression significantly inhibited RGC apoptosis in strip1rw147 mutants.
source: Bcl2 overexpression significantly inhibited RGC apoptosis in strip1rw147 mutants (Figure 7A, B).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 7A, B.

claim: At 78 hpf, RGCs were partially but significantly recovered in strip1rw147 mutants overexpressing Bcl2, compared to non-transgenic mutants.
source: Accordingly, at 78 hpf, RGCs were partially but significantly recovered in strip1rw147 mutants overexpressing Bcl2, compared to non-transgenic mutants (Figure 7C, D).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 7C, D.

claim: Loss of RGCs in strip1rw147 mutants depends on the mitochondria-mediated apoptotic pathway.
source: Thus, loss of RGCs in strip1rw147 mutants depends on the mitochondria-mediated apoptotic pathway.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Results and supported by Bcl2 rescue experiments.

claim: strip1rw147 mutants overexpressing Bcl2 still displayed IPL defects.
source: Surprisingly, strip1rw147 mutants overexpressing Bcl2 still displayed IPL defects.
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results.

claim: In Bcl2-rescued strip1rw147 mutants, the IPL was not formed at the interface between surviving RGCs and ACs, but instead, a thin IPL-like neuropil was ectopically formed in the middle of presumptive AC layer.
source: In this case, the IPL was not formed at the interface between surviving RGCs and ACs, but instead, a thin IPL-like neuropil was ectopically formed in the middle of presumptive AC layer (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Surviving RGCs in strip1rw147 mutants apparently fail to project their dendrites to the IPL-like thin neuropil.
source: In addition, surviving RGCs in strip1rw147 mutants apparently fail to project their dendrites to the IPL-like thin neuropil, consistent with our previous findings on the cell autonomous role of Strip1 in RGC neurite patterning.
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the Results.

claim: Strip1 performs multiple functions in development of inner retinal neural circuit.
source: Using zebrafish, we demonstrate that Strip1 performs multiple functions in development of inner retinal neural circuit.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by all experimental data.

claim: Strip1 suppresses Jun-mediated proapoptotic signaling in RGCs during development, probably through the STRIPAK complex.
source: First, we discovered a novel neuroprotective mechanism governed by Strip1, probably through the STRIPAK complex, to suppress Jun-mediated proapoptotic signaling in RGCs during development (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data.

claim: Strip1-mediated RGC maintenance is essential for laminar positioning of other retinal neurons and structural integrity of the IPL.
source: In addition, we demonstrate that Strip1-mediated RGC maintenance is essential for laminar positioning of other retinal neurons and structural integrity of the IPL.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data.

claim: Around 50% of mammalian RGCs undergo apoptotic cell death during development.
source: Unlike zebrafish retina, in which only 1.06% of RGCs die during development (Biehlmaier et al., 2001), around 50% of mammalian RGCs undergo apoptotic cell death (Bähr, 2000; Fawcett et al., 1984).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The survival rate of mouse RGCs following ONI is only ~8% compared to a survival rate of ~75% of zebrafish RGCs.
source: Similarly, the survival rate of mouse RGCs following ONI is only ~8% compared to a survival rate of ~75% of zebrafish RGCs (Li et al., 2020; Zou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Loss of zebrafish Strip1 causes an elevated apoptotic stress response profile in embryonic retinas having a degree of overlap with adult RGCs post-ONI.
source: Interestingly, loss of zebrafish Strip1 causes an elevated apoptotic stress response profile in embryonic retinas having a degree of overlap with adult RGCs post-ONI.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by RNA-seq data.

claim: Five out of the six overlapping upregulated markers (jun, atf3, stmn4, sox11b, and adcyap1b) are commonly upregulated in retinal transcriptomic studies of mammalian ONI models.
source: Indeed, five out of the six overlapping upregulated markers (jun, atf3, stmn4, sox11b, and adcyap1b) are commonly upregulated in retinal transcriptomic studies of mammalian ONI models (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: JNK/Jun activation is a major cause of axonal injury- or glaucoma-induced RGC death.
source: Jun is the canonical target of JNK signaling and JNK/Jun activation is a major cause of axonal injury- or glaucoma-induced RGC death (Fernandes et al., 2012; Fernandes et al., 2013; Syc-Mazurek et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Jun signaling appears to be a common mediator of RGC death among vertebrates.
source: Thus, Jun signaling appears to be a common mediator of RGC death among vertebrates.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by comparative analysis of transcriptomic data.

claim: Strip1 is cell autonomously required for both RGC survival and RGC neurite patterning.
source: We reported that Strip1 is cell autonomously required for both RGC survival and RGC neurite patterning.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by cell transplantation data.

claim: The Jun-mediated apoptotic program starts as early as 48 hpf in strip1 mutants.
source: Our data at cellular and molecular levels show that the Jun-mediated apoptotic program starts as early as 48 hpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by immunostaining data.

claim: RGCs start to project apical dendrites and innervate the IPL at around 55–60 hpf, following lamination cues from ACs.
source: On the other hand, previous reports suggest that RGCs start to project apical dendrites and innervate the IPL at around 55–60 hpf, following lamination cues from ACs (Choi et al., 2010; Mumm et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Synaptogenesis in the IPL starts at around 60 hpf.
source: In addition, synaptogenesis in the IPL starts at around 60 hpf (Schmitt and Dowling, 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: It is unlikely that failure of connectivity in the IPL is the primary cause of RGC death in strip1 mutants.
source: Therefore, it is unlikely that failure of connectivity in the IPL is the primary cause of RGC death.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by temporal analysis of RGC death and IPL formation.

claim: In wild-type zebrafish embryos, complete optic nerve transection in 5-dpf larvae does not induce prominent RGC death.
source: In wild-type zebrafish embryos, complete optic nerve transection in 5-dpf larvae does not induce prominent RGC death (Harvey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Recruitment of many STRIPAK components is compromised in strip1 mutants.
source: Our proteomic assays revealed that recruitment of many STRIPAK components is compromised in strip1 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by Co-IP/MS data.

claim: STRIP1 and STRN3 are organizing centers for the STRIPAK complex and their mutant forms compromise complex assembly and function.
source: Recently, several studies on the human STRIPAK complex found that STRIP1 and STRN3 are organizing centers for the STRIPAK complex and that their mutant forms compromise complex assembly and function (Jeong et al., 2021; Tang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MAP4 kinases activate the JNK signaling pathway and they are among kinase family members that are recruited and dephosphorylated by the STRIPAK complex.
source: MAP4 kinases activate the JNK signaling pathway and they are among kinase family members that are recruited and dephosphorylated by the STRIPAK complex (Fuller et al., 2021; Hwang and Pallas, 2014; Kim et al., 2020; Seo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: JNK signaling is activated in STRIP1/2-knockout human cell lines.
source: Moreover, JNK signaling is activated in STRIP1/2-knockout human cell lines (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The interaction between Strip and CKa suppresses JNK signaling in Drosophila testis.
source: Similarly, the interaction between Strip and CKa (Drosophila homolog of Striatins) suppresses JNK signaling in Drosophila testis (La marca, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: It is likely that Strip1 and Strn3 function in the context of the STRIPAK complex to modulate JNK/Jun activity, thereby promoting RGC survival.
source: Thus, it is likely that Strip1 and Strn3 function in the context of the STRIPAK complex to modulate JNK/Jun activity, thereby promoting RGC survival.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data and prior literature.

claim: This study is the first in vivo evidence for a functional interaction between STRIPAK components and Jun signaling in vertebrates.
source: To our knowledge, this study is the first in vivo evidence for a functional interaction between STRIPAK components and Jun signaling in vertebrates.
evidence: This is a claim stated in the Discussion based on the novelty of the findings.

claim: Upon genetic elimination of different inner retinal cells, the remaining cells manage to form an IPL-like neuropil.
source: Upon genetic elimination of different inner retinal cells, the remaining cells manage to form an IPL-like neuropil (Randlett et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: ACs play the dominant role in IPL initiation.
source: However, it is widely agreed that ACs play the dominant role in IPL initiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as established knowledge.

claim: ACs project their neurites to form a proto-IPL.
source: Elegant time-lapse experiments show that ACs project their neurites to form a proto-IPL (Chow et al., 2015; Godinho et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: RGC death in strip1 mutants is strongly linked to abnormal infiltration of ACs and BPs in the GCL and the perturbed IPL.
source: We found that RGC death in strip1 mutants is strongly linked to abnormal infiltration of ACs and BPs in the GCL and the perturbed IPL.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data.

claim: In knockout mice in which atypical Cadherin Fat3 is absent in both RGCs and ACs, ACs invade the GCL abnormally.
source: In knockout mice in which atypical Cadherin Fat3 is absent in both RGCs and ACs, ACs invade the GCL abnormally.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: AC-specific Fat3 knockout mice do not exhibit AC positioning defects.
source: However, AC-specific knockout mice do not exhibit such positioning defects (Deans et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: RGCs provide positional cues for migrating ACs to initiate a proper IPL program, whereas ACs subsequently project their dendritic plexuses to establish the foundation for a proto-IPL.
source: Therefore, we reintroduce a model proposed by Kay et al., 2004, in which both RGCs and ACs play distinct roles in shaping the developing IPL. In this model, RGCs provide positional cues for migrating ACs to initiate a proper IPL program, whereas ACs subsequently project their dendritic plexuses to establish the foundation for a proto-IPL.
evidence: This is a model proposed in the Discussion based on experimental data and prior literature.

claim: Bcl2-rescued strip1 mutants show defects in dendritic patterns of surviving RGCs, which are associated with an ectopic IPL formed amidst presumptive ACs.
source: However, Bcl2-rescued strip1 mutants provide valuable new insights into such mechanisms. Bcl2-rescued mutants show defects in dendritic patterns of surviving RGCs, which are associated with an ectopic IPL formed amidst presumptive ACs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: RGCs serve dual functions in IPL development: (1) RGCs act as a physical barrier that prevents abnormal infiltration of ACs into the GCL and (2) RGCs show dendritic guidance cues that establish interactions between RGCs and ACs for a proper IPL program.
source: Thus, we propose that RGCs serve dual functions in IPL development (summarized in Figure 8B): (1) RGCs act as a physical barrier that prevents abnormal infiltration of ACs into the GCL and (2) RGCs show dendritic guidance cues that establish interactions between RGCs and ACs for a proper IPL program.
evidence: This is a model proposed in the Discussion based on experimental data.

claim: A hypomorphic allele of zebrafish n-cadherin mutants compromises IPL formation with abnormal neurite patterning of INL cells.
source: A hypomorphic allele of zebrafish n-cadherin mutants compromises IPL formation with abnormal neurite patterning of INL cells (Masai et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In Xenopus, Nrp1 and PlexinA1 inhibition induced randomly oriented dendritic patterning of RGCs, similar to zebrafish strip1 mutants.
source: In Xenopus, Nrp1 and PlexinA1 inhibition induced randomly oriented dendritic patterning of RGCs, similar to zebrafish strip1 mutants (Kita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Strip1 is required for proper neurite patterning of RGCs, and probably small subsets of ACs and BPs.
source: Lastly, we show that Strip1 is required for proper neurite patterning of RGCs, and probably small subsets of ACs and BPs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data.

claim: Drosophila Strip has established roles in dendritic branching and axon elongation.
source: This is supported by established roles of Drosophila Strip in dendritic branching and axon elongation (Sakuma et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A series of Strip1-mediated regulatory mechanisms constructs retinal neural circuit through RGC survival and neurite patterning of retinal neurons.
source: In summary, we demonstrate that a series of Strip1-mediated regulatory mechanisms constructs retinal neural circuit through RGC survival and neurite patterning of retinal neurons.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by all experimental data.
